record.title: Highly solvable knots with large 4-genera.
record.statement: For arbitrary $n>2$ and $g>0$ prove that there exist $n$-solvable knots $K$ such that the topological 4-genus of $K$ is strictly more than $g$.
record.source_name: AimPL: Smooth concordance classes of topologically slice knots (posed by Jae Choon Cha)

record.title: Concordance of knots in homology spheres.
record.statement: Is every knot in every integer homology sphere topologically concordant in some integer homology cobordism to a knot in $S^3$? (i.e. is $\phi_{top}$ surjective?)
record.source_name: AimPL: Smooth concordance classes of topologically slice knots (posed by Christopher Davis)

record.title: Branched covers and concordance
record.statement: Suppose $K$ and $J$ are knots in $S^3$ such that for every prime power $q$, the $q$th cyclic branched covers $\Sigma_q(K)$ and $\Sigma_q(J)$ are rationally homology cobordant. Must $K$ and $J$ be concordant?
record.source_name: AimPL: Smooth concordance classes of topologically slice knots

record.title: Surgeries and concordance
record.statement: Suppose $K$ and $J$ are knots in $S^3$ such that for all $p/q \in \mathbb{Q}$, the Dehn surgeries $S^3_{p/q}(K)$ and $S^3_{p/q}(J)$ are integer homology cobordant. Must $K$ and $J$ be concordant?
record.source_name: AimPL: Smooth concordance classes of topologically slice knots

record.title: It's known that the group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms on … is perfect.
record.statement: It's known that the group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms on $S^3$ is perfect. Is the commutator length uniformly bounded?
record.source_name: AimPL: Floer theory of symmetric products and Hilbert schemes (posed by Tsuboi-Polterovich)

record.statement: Is $\displaystyle \frac{\text{FPdim}(\mathcal{C})}{\text{FPdim}(X)}$ an algebraic integer for every $X\in\text{Irr}(\mathcal{C})$?

record.statement: Is there a conceptual construction of the even half of 4442?

record.title: Problems in Low Forcing (problem 4)
record.statement: Is it consistent to have $\lim^p \mathbb{A} = 0$ for all $p$?
record.source_name: AimPL: High and Low forcing (posed by Justin Moore)

record.title: Problems in Low Forcing (problem 9)
record.statement: The following is inconsistent: “For every $\Sigma_1$ statement $\varphi$ with $\aleph_1$ and $\aleph_2$ as parameters, if $\varphi$ can be forced by an $\aleph_1, \aleph_2$-preserving forcing, then $\varphi$ holds.”

record.title: Problems in Low Forcing (problem 10)
record.statement: Do any of the analogs of PFA at $\aleph_2$ give us $|X| \le 2^{\aleph_1}$ for every Hausdorff space with no discrete subspaces of size $\aleph_2$?
record.source_name: AimPL: High and Low forcing (posed by Stevo Todorčević)

record.title: Problems in High Forcing (problem 1)
record.statement: Is it consistent (relative to large cardinals) that $\text{TP}_{\aleph_{\omega+1}}$ holds along with reflection for all stationary subsets of $\aleph_{\omega+1}$?

record.title: Effective Jumps (problem 2)
record.statement: Given an equivalence relation $E$ on $X$ and a countable group $G$, define an equivalence relation on $X^G$ by $\alpha E^{[G]} \beta$ iff there is some $g\in G$ such that for every $h\in G$, we have $\alpha(g^{-1} h) E \beta(h)$. For which $E$ and $G$ is $E < E^{[G]}$? What about the effective versions of this problem?

record.title: Classify real linear combinations of products of minors that are nonnegative for all … matrices.
record.source_name: AimPL: Theory and applications of total positivity (posed by Prateek Kumar Vishwakarma)

record.title: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.2
record.statement: Let $S$ be a finite simple group, and let $G$ be a finite group for which there exists a bijection $f:G\to S$ such that $|x|$ divides $|f(x)|$ for all $x\in G$. Must $G$ necessarily be simple?

record.title: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.10
record.statement: We call a group presentation finite if it represents a finite group. We say that a presentation is just finite if it is finite and is no longer finite on removal of any relation from it. Is it true that every finite group has a just finite presentation?

record.title: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.24
record.statement: For a finite group G, the power graph P(G) is the graph with vertex set G and edges \{x, y\} for all $x\ne y\in G$ such that either $x\in\langle y\rangle$ or $y\in\langle x\rangle$. Is it true that, for every finite group G, if P(G) is a cograph, then P(G) is chordal?

record.title: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.26
record.statement: Let $G$ be a non-trivial finite group and let $p_1,\ldots,p_k$ be the distinct prime divisors of $|G|$. For each $i$, let $H_i$ be a Sylow $p_i$-subgroup of $G$. Is it true that there exists an element $x\in G$ such that for all $i$ the subgroup $H_i\cap H_i^x$ is inclusion-minimal in $\{H_i\cap H_i^g:g\in G\}$?

record.title: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.28
record.statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple transitive permutation group, and let $\delta(G)$ be the proportion of derangements in $G$. Is it true that $\delta(G)\geqslant 89/325$?

record.title: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.29
record.statement: Let $G\leqslant\operatorname{Sym}(\Omega)$ be a finite primitive permutation group with a regular suborbit (that is, $G$ has a trivial 2-point stabiliser). Then is it true that for all $\alpha,\beta\in\Omega$, there exists $\gamma\in\Omega$ such that the 2-point stabilisers $G_{\alpha,\gamma}$ and $G_{\beta,\gamma}$ are both trivial?

record.title: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.50
record.statement:
Does every finite 3-group $T$ have a nontrivial characteristic subgroup $C$ such that if $T$ is a Sylow 3-subgroup of a finite group $G$, then $T\cap G'=T\cap H'$, where $H=N_G(C)$?

The group $S_4$ shows that no such characteristic subgroups can be found in some Sylow 2-subgroups.

record.title: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.58
record.statement: We say that a product $XY=\{xy\mid x\in X,\ y\in Y\}$ of two subsets $X,Y$ of a group $G$ is direct if for every $z\in XY$ there are unique $x\in X$, $y\in Y$ such that $z=xy$. Is there an infinite group $G$ such that every subset $A\subseteq G$ satisfies the following property: all the maximal subsets $B$ for which the product $AB$ is direct have the same cardinality?

record.title: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.66
record.statement:
Suppose that A is a nilpotent group of automorphisms of a finite soluble group G. Is the Fitting height of G bounded in terms of |A| and |CG(A)|?

Isaacs), when A is cyclic (see 19.43), or when CG(A) = 1 (E. C. Dade).

record.title: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.68
record.statement:
A finite group $G$ is said to be semi-abelian if it has a sequence of subgroups $1=G_0\leqslant G_1\leqslant\cdots\leqslant G_n=G$ such that for every $i$ the subgroup $G_{i+1}$ is isomorphic to a quotient of a semidirect product $A_i\rtimes G_i$ for some abelian group $A_i$.

Conjecture: Semi-abelian finite groups are monomial.

record.title: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.86
record.statement: A group $G$ is said to be sofic if for every finite set $F\subseteq G$ containing $1$ and every $\varepsilon>0$ there exist $n\in\mathbb N$ and a map $\phi:F\to S_n$ such that $\phi(1)=1$, $d(\phi(gh),\phi(g)\phi(h))<\varepsilon$ for all $g,h$ such that $gh\in F$, and $\phi(g)$ does not have fixed points for every $g\in F\setminus\{1\}$. Is every group sofic?

record.title: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.88
record.statement: Is there a finite non-abelian group $G$ of odd order, with $k(G)$ conjugacy classes, such that $k(G)/|G|=1/17$?

record.title: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.89
record.statement: For $n>39$, is it true that the number of conjugacy classes in the symmetric group $S_n$ of degree $n$ is never a divisor of the order of $S_n$? In other words, is it true that, for $n>39$, the number $p(n)$ of integer partitions of $n$ is never a divisor of $n!$?

record.title: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.103
record.statement: A Hausdorff topological group G is called minimal if it does not admit a strictly coarser Hausdorff group topology. A topological group is called Raikov complete if its two-sided uniform structure is complete. Is it true that an arbitrary Cartesian product of Raikov complete minimal topological groups remains minimal?

record.title: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.107
record.statement: A sequence $\{F_n\}$ of pairwise disjoint finite subsets of a topological group is called expansive if for every open subset $U$ there is a number $m$ such that $F_n\cap U\ne\emptyset$ for all $n>m$. Suppose that a countable group $G$ can be partitioned into countably many dense subsets. Is it true that in $G$ there exists an expansive sequence?

record.title: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.108
record.statement: For a finite group $G$ let $\operatorname{Cod}(G)$ denote the set of irreducible character codegrees of $G$ (see 20.78). Define $\sigma(G)=\max\{|\pi(m)|:m\in\operatorname{Cod}(G)\}$, where $\pi(m)$ denotes the set of prime divisors of an integer $m$. Can the constant $k$ be taken as 4?

record.title: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.114
record.statement: A finite group G is called weakly ab-maximal if |H : [H, H]| $\leqslant$ |G : [G, G]| for all H $\leqslant$ G. Do weakly ab-maximal groups have bounded derived length?

record.title: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.117
record.statement:
(a) Does there exist a finitely generated simple group that is of exponential growth but not of uniformly exponential growth?

(b) Does there exist a finitely generated hereditarily just-infinite group that is of exponential growth but not of uniformly exponential growth?

record.title: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.119
record.statement: Does there exist a group $G$ that contains a family $(G_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ of finite-index subgroups such that for every $n$ there is a homomorphism $f_n:G_n\to\mathbb Z$ whose kernel is of type $F_n$, but not of type $F_{n+1}$?

record.title: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.127
record.statement: Let G be a right-angled Artin group. Is the stable commutator length scl(g) a rational number for every g $\in$ [G, G]?

record.title: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.142
record.statement: A group $G$ is said to be invariably generated by $a$ and $b$ if $G$ is generated by the conjugates $a^g,b^h$ for every $g,h$. Let $p\ne q$ be fixed primes. Does every finite group embed into a finite group invariably generated by an element of order $p$ and an element of order $q$?

record.title: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 1.10
record.statement: (Canary) Let $G$ be word-hyperbolic and $H$ a finitely presented subgroup of $G$. Suppose that for every $g\in G$ there is $n>0$ such that $g^n\in H$. Does it follow that $H$ has finite index in $G$?
record.source_name: Bestvina - Questions in Geometric Group Theory (pdf) (2004)

record.title: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 2.18
record.statement: (Ross Geoghegan) A proper CAT(0) space $M$ is almost geodesically complete if there is $R\geq0$ such that for all $a,b\in M$ there is an infinite geodesic ray starting at $a$ and passing within $R$ of $b$. If $\operatorname{Isom}(M)$ acts cocompactly on $M$, is $M$ almost geodesically complete?
record.source_name: Bestvina - Questions in Geometric Group Theory (pdf) (2004)

record.title: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 8.10
record.statement: Suppose $H=F/N$ is finitely presented and contains $C^n$ for every $n$. Write $G_n=H*_{C^n}H=F*F/N_n$. If $C$ is nontrivial and finite, is $$\lim_{n\to\infty}d_{F*F}(N_n)=\infty?$$
record.source_name: Bestvina - Questions in Geometric Group Theory (pdf) (2004)

record.title: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 10.2
record.statement: (Belegredek) Is there a 3-complex X (not necessarily aspherical) which is not homotopy equivalent to a 2-complex but H³(X; {G}) = 0 for all local coefficients?
record.source_name: Bestvina - Questions in Geometric Group Theory (pdf) (2004)

record.title: Questions in Geometric Group Theory — Q 13.3
record.statement: (Henry Glover) Does for every finite graph G the following 1−2−∞- conjecture hold: G is planar, a double cover of G is planar, or no finite cover is planar?
record.source_name: Bestvina - Questions in Geometric Group Theory (pdf) (2004)

record.title: Some Questions — Question 14
record.statement: Compactness implies that for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $K>0$ such that every finite graph can be approximated within error $\varepsilon$ by a finite graph of size $K$. Give an estimate for $K$ in terms of $\varepsilon$.

record.title: Some Questions — Question 15
record.statement: Let $(G_n)$ be a locally convergent graph sequence and let $\mu_n$ be the probability distribution of the roots of the chromatic polynomial of $G_n$. For every $k$, does $\lim_{n\to\infty}\int_{\mathbb{C}}z^k\,d\mu_n$ exist?

record.title: Some Questions — Question 18
record.statement: For each $d\geq3$, does the independence ratio of a uniformly random $d$-regular graph converge in probability as the number of vertices tends to infinity?

record.title: Some Questions — Question 19
record.statement: Do uniformly random $d$-regular graphs converge, in local-global convergence, to the weak closure of independent identically distributed processes?

record.title: Some Questions — Question 33
record.statement: For every $k>1$, does there exist $C(k)<1$ such that the return probability of every transient $k$-regular Cayley graph is at most $C(k)$?

record.title: Some Questions — Question 45
record.statement: Let an amenable group $\Gamma$ act ergodically and essentially faithfully on $X$. Is the groupoid cost of the action $1$? If $\Gamma$ is finitely presented, is this true for every infinite ergodic action?

record.title: Algebraic Stories — Hilbert series of generic power ideals.
record.statement: [Fr\"oberg-Iarrobino Conjecture] Given generic linear forms $\ell_1, \ldots, \ell_r$ and a positive integer $d$, let $I$ be the power ideal generated by $\ell_1^d,\ldots,\ell_r^d$. Then the Hilbert function of $R = S/I$ is as in [source label: eq:RALF], except for the cases $(n,r) = (3,7), (3,8), (4,9), (5,14)$ and possibly for $r = n+2$ and $r = n+3$.
record.source_name: Fröberg, Lundqvist, Oneto, Shapiro - Algebraic Stories from One and from the Other Pockets (2018)
